verdict.rationale: Inngest documents event-triggered function runs: events can trigger runs, and rate-limited events 'do not trigger functions to start'. It also documents first-party webhook consumer URLs for third-party services such as Stripe and GitHub. The evidence does not show declarative trigger configuration, external queues as a trigger source, or one event fanning out to many functions. missing for 10: explicit fan-out of one event to multiple functions, declarative trigger definition docs, queue-sourced triggers, independent corroboration of event-trigger behavior

support.subject: As a backend developer, events from my app, webhooks, or queues trigger workflows declaratively, and one event can fan out to many functions

citations.quote: Inngest enables you to create any number of unique URLs which act as webhook consumers. You can create a webhook for each third party service that you use (e.g. Stripe, Github, Clerk)
Any run triggered by another run (via event, invoke, or defer) inherits its parent's sessions.
Events that exceed the rate limit are skipped and do not trigger functions to start.
